metadata.case_name: NG YU FU v. WONG SHEK MING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Operated his own company called Fu Shing Engineering Co. from 1989 dealing with business of installation repair and maintenance of air-conditioners

injuries.description: the Plaintiff had only suffered a back contusion
source: the Plaintiff had only suffered a back contusion

“He was well on examination and walking unaided. His back was tender on the sacral region and there was no neurology identified. X-ray lumbo-sacral spine was taken, which was normal. He was given analgesic and topical ointment. Sick leave from 7/5/2001 to 10/5/2001 was granted.” (Dr. Lee’s report dated 6 January 2002)
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of lower back or pelvis

injuries.description: multiple levels of very mild posterior disc bulges / slight posterior bulging of degenerated lower lumbar disc
source: It is difficult to interpret the multiple levels of very mild posterior disc bulges as described in the MRI findings.
Dr. Kenneth Ho’s report (p71) stating ‘There was posterior herniations of the degenerated lower lumber disc, slight posterior bulging ……'.
Dr. Chun had stated categorically that this was not a disc prolapse but a bulge. He cited high authority for the proposition that bulging of disc is age related and not caused by trauma.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: His back was tender on the sacral region
episode paraethesia in lower limbs during walking
moderate limitation in the SLR test
mild limitation in the end of range of movement of back
no obvious motor neurological deficit in the lower limbs and reflexes were normal
even with described ache at the end of range of back motion, the overall range of movement of back was still considered as reasonably preserved

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenity
